title: File BL-27: a run with no transcripts reports success and projects zero cost
body:
Files **BL-27**, a defect measured this session against the corpus the
2026-08-20 local-lane run left on disk.

`select` ran twelve minutes before `fetch` finished writing
`data/transcripts/`. It wrote 285 rows, every one carrying `"mentions":[]`,
and printed no warning. `estimate` then read that file and printed a
zero-character, zero-token projection ending in R7's checkpoint sentence,
"The pipeline STOPS here" — the same output a healthy, finished run produces.
Re-running `select` against the complete cache produced 89 threshold passes,
198 selected videos and 650 bundles, so nothing was wrong with the corpus or
the code: only the order, and nothing said so.

**R1005 (OD-9) does not cover this.** No artifact was missing. The absent
input was the transcript cache, which the design deliberately tolerates per
video — `commands/estimate.py` says so — because a title-hit video may have no
caption track and R24's ledger owns that case. What is unstated is the
population case: tolerating one absent transcript and tolerating all 285 are
different judgements sharing one code path.

Evidence only. No requirement, no plan, no code — this is the ledger entry the
decision that follows will cite, landed first so it resolves at that pull
request's base commit.
